motivation: The full-data standardized N_eff coefficient remains highly unusual under year-block permutation, but both predictor and response use the same census at year t. Test whether shared census-count error and small-colony zeroing can mechanically generate an observed-scale positive coefficient when the latent year-specific topology-growth alignment has been destroyed.

latent_null.total_abundance: retain the observed island-year total as the latent expected total
latent_null.colony_composition: replace each target island-year composition with the same island's composition from a year-block-permuted donor year, using the identical five-island/four-island strata frozen in PALMER_NEFF_YEAR_BLOCK_PERMUTATION_V1
latent_null.effect: destroys latent year-specific N_eff to next-year-growth alignment while retaining island identity, broad availability phase, target abundance trajectory, and within-year donor-block topology structure

primary_error_model.name: independent Poisson colony counts
primary_error_model.construction: For each target start island-year, draw colony counts independently as Poisson(target observed total × donor-year colony shares). If a state known occupied in the frozen data is drawn as total zero, resample that state until total > 0.
primary_error_model.rationale: stylized lower-bound count-noise model; not claimed to be an empirically calibrated observer-error distribution

paired_coupling_design.coupled: derive N_eff_t and current_total_t from the same simulated colony-count vector A; derive next_total_t+1 from independent total draw B
paired_coupling_design.decoupled: derive N_eff_t from simulated vector A but current_total_t and next_total_t+1 from independent total draws B
paired_coupling_design.shared_next_draw: the same B next-year total is used in coupled and decoupled fits within each replicate
paired_coupling_design.target_quantity: paired difference beta_coupled - beta_decoupled isolates the expected coefficient shift caused by sharing current-year count error between N_eff and the growth denominator/baseline abundance

model: same full-data C1 coefficient model: next_growth ~ island fixed effects + z(log1p current abundance) + z(year) + z(log1p N_eff)
primary_outputs: coupled beta null distribution and one-sided probability beta >= observed beta
decoupled beta null distribution and one-sided probability beta >= observed beta
median coupling bias as a fraction of observed beta
proportion of coupled and decoupled coefficients > 0

fixed_sensitivities.definition: each positive colony mean is multiplied by an independent Gamma factor with mean 1 and CV 0.10 before the Poisson draw
each positive colony mean is multiplied by an independent Gamma factor with mean 1 and CV 0.20 before the Poisson draw

interpretation_rules.mechanical_generation_concerning: observed beta is not unusual (one-sided p > 0.05) in the coupled topology-null simulation
interpretation_rules.shared_error_bias_material: report the paired bias magnitude relative to observed beta; do not impose a post hoc threshold
interpretation_rules.coefficient_survives_this_diagnostic: observed beta remains unusual (p <= 0.05) under all three predeclared error models and paired coupling bias is small relative to the observed beta

boundaries: This is a post-positive diagnostic, not independent biological replication.
Poisson and fixed 10%/20% overdispersion are stylized count-error sensitivities, not estimates of Palmer census observer error.
No alternative CV grid, noise family, topology metric, or coefficient threshold may be selected after simulation results are opened.
The held-out predictive gain already failed year-block permutation and is not rescued by this coefficient diagnostic.
manuscript_consequence: If the coefficient survives, it may remain only as a conditional same-census association with explicit uncertainty; if it fails, remove N_eff as a biological result rather than retuning the topology model.
